translations.literal: Treatise Nineteen: Geography Two
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 19: Geography 2

sentences.zh: ○河東道三河北道四山南道五河東道河中府府，隋河東郡。

translations.literal: ○ Hedong Circuit 3, Hebei Circuit 4, Shannan Circuit 5. Hedong Circuit: Hedong Prefecture; Hedong Superior Prefecture, the Sui Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Hedong Circuit 3, Hebei Circuit 4, Shannan Circuit 5. Hedong Circuit — Hedong Superior Prefecture: in Sui times the Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: ，置蒲州，治桑泉縣，領河東、桑泉、猗氏、虞鄉四縣。

translations.literal: , Pu Prefecture was established, administering Sangquan County, and overseeing Hedong, Sangquan, Yishi, and Yuxiang—four counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Pu Prefecture was established with its seat at Sangquan County, governing Hedong, Sangquan, Yishi, and Yuxiang.

sentences.zh: 二年，置蒲州總管府，管蒲、虞、泰、絳、邵、澮六州。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Pu Prefecture Superintendency was established, overseeing Pu, Yu, Tai, Jiang, Shao, and Huan—six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, a superintendency for Pu Prefecture was set up, supervising Pu, Yu, Tai, Jiang, Shao, and Huan.

sentences.zh: 三年，移蒲治河東縣，依舊總管府。

translations.literal: In the third year, Pu was moved to administer Hedong County, retaining the superintendency as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the prefectural seat was moved to Hedong County, while the superintendency remained unchanged.

translations.literal: That same year, Wenquan County was established.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wenquan County was also established.

sentences.zh: 九年，又置都督府，管蒲、虞、芮、邵、泰五州，仍省溫泉縣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, a military commission was again established, overseeing Pu, Yu, Rui, Shao, and Tai—five prefectures—and Wenquan County was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year a regional military commission was re-established over Pu, Yu, Rui, Shao, and Tai, and Wenquan County was abolished again.

translations.literal: That same year, the military commission was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the commission was dissolved.

translations.literal: , Yongle from Guo Prefecture was detached and placed under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenguan, Yongle County was detached from Guo Prefecture and assigned to Pu.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以廢虞州之安邑解縣、廢泰州之汾陰來屬。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Anyi and Jie from the abolished Yu Prefecture and Fenyin from the abolished Tai Prefecture were placed under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Anyi and Jie from the abolished Yu Prefecture and Fenyin from the abolished Tai Prefecture were added.

translations.literal: , the Central Capital was established and Pu Prefecture was changed to the Hedong Superior Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan, the Central Capital was established and Pu Prefecture was redesignated Hedong Superior Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其年，罷中都，依舊為蒲州，又與陝，鄭、汴、懷、魏為「六雄」。

translations.literal: That same year, the Central Capital was abolished and it reverted to Pu Prefecture; it was also grouped with Shan, Zheng, Bian, Huai, and Wei as the "Six Great Powers."
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Central Capital was abolished and the seat reverted to Pu Prefecture; together with Shan, Zheng, Bian, Huai, and Wei it ranked among the "Six Great Powers."

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, it was promoted to one of the "Four Aides."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan it was elevated to one of the "Four Aides."

translations.literal: , it was changed to the Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao it was renamed the Hedong commandery.

translations.literal: , it was restored as Pu Prefecture, and Anyi was detached to belong to Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan it again became Pu Prefecture, and Anyi was transferred to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，置河中府，析同州之朝邑，於河西鹽坊置河西縣，來屬。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, the Hedong Superior Prefecture was established; Chaoyi from Tong Prefecture was detached, and Hexi County was established at the Hexi salt works on the west bank of the river and placed under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Qianyuan, Hedong Superior Prefecture was restored; Chaoyi was taken from Tong Prefecture, Hexi County was created at the west-bank salt works, and both were placed under the prefecture.

translations.literal: In the first year, in the jianmao month, it again became the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the jianmao month of the first year of Guangde it was again made the Central Capital.

translations.literal: , it was restored as the Hedong Superior Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai it was again restored as Hedong Superior Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣五，戶三萬六千四百九十九，口十七萬三千七百八十四。

translations.literal: Formerly it oversaw five counties, with 36,499 households and 173,784 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly it governed five counties, with 36,499 households and a population of 173,784.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣八，戶七萬八百，口四十六萬九千二百一十三。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it oversaw eight counties, with 70,800 households and 469,213 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao it governed eight counties, with 70,800 households and 469,213 persons.

translations.literal: Under Yuanhe it oversaw eleven counties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanhe it governed eleven counties.

sentences.zh: 在京師東北三百二十四里，去東都五百五十里。

translations.literal: It lay 324 li northeast of the capital and 550 li from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It stood 324 li northeast of Chang'an and 550 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: A Sui county.
translations.idiomatic: A county of Sui times.

translations.literal: Seat of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It served as the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: , Hexi County was established by detachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan, Hexi County was established by division.

translations.literal: That same year the Central Capital was abolished; it was then abolished [again], and [later] restored.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the Central Capital was abolished, the county was abolished as well; in the third year of Qianyuan it was restored.

sentences.zh: 舊朝邑縣，屬同州，管長春宮。

translations.literal: Formerly Chaoyi County, subordinate to Tong Prefecture, administering the Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Chaoyi County under Tong Prefecture, which oversaw the Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: ，置河中府，割朝邑來屬，改為河西縣，以鹽坊為理所

translations.literal: , the Hedong Superior Prefecture was established; Chaoyi was detached and placed under it, changed to Hexi County, with the salt works as the seat of administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan, when Hedong Superior Prefecture was established, Chaoyi was transferred, renamed Hexi County, and the salt works became its seat.

translations.literal: In Sui, Sangquan County was established by detaching from Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, Sangquan County was split off from Yishi.

translations.literal: , Wenquan County was established by detachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wude, Wenquan County was established by division.

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Wenquan was abolished and merged into Sangquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Wude, Wenquan was abolished and merged into Sangquan.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Linjin County.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao it was renamed Linjin County.

translations.literal: Sui Yuxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: A county of Sui times, Yuxiang.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Jie County and placed under Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude it was renamed Jie County and assigned to Yu Prefecture.

translations.literal: Pu Prefecture separately established Yuxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Prefecture then established a separate Yuxiang County.

translations.literal: , Jie County was abolished and merged into Yuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Jie County was abolished and merged into Yuxiang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，復析置解縣，屬蒲州

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Jie County was again established by detachment and placed under Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan, Jie County was re-established and assigned to Pu Prefecture.

translations.literal: A Han county—the ancient state of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: A Han county on the site of the ancient state of Xun.

sentences.zh: 漢解縣地，後魏分置虞鄉縣。

translations.literal: Territory of Han Jie County; in Later Wei, Yuxiang County was established by detachment.
translations.idiomatic: On the ground of Han Jie County; in Later Wei, Yuxiang County was split off.

translations.literal: , Jie County was abolished and merged into Yuxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Jie County was abolished and merged into Yuxiang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，復置解縣，省虞鄉。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Jie County was restored and Yuxiang was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, Jie County was restored and Yuxiang was abolished.

translations.literal: , Jie County was again detached to establish Yuxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou, Jie County was again divided to re-establish Yuxiang County.

translations.literal: , Ruicheng County was established by detachment and placed under Rui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Ruicheng County was split off and assigned to Rui Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Rui Prefecture was abolished and it was changed to belong to Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Wude, Rui Prefecture was abolished and the county was placed under Ding Prefecture.

translations.literal: , it was changed to belong to Pu Prefecture, then again detached to belong to Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenguan it was assigned to Pu Prefecture, then later transferred to Guo Prefecture.

translations.literal: , it again came under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong it was again placed under Pu.

translations.literal: Han Fenyin County.
translations.idiomatic: The Han county of Fenyin.

translations.literal: Under the Sui it belonged to Tai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui it belonged to Tai Prefecture.

translations.literal: , Tai Prefecture was abolished and the county came under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, when Tai Prefecture was abolished, the county was assigned here.

sentences.zh: ，玄宗祀後土，獲寶鼎，因改為寶鼎

translations.literal: , the Emperor Xuanzong sacrificed to the Earth Queen and obtained the precious tripod; therefore it was changed to Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, when Emperor Xuanzong sacrificed to the Earth Queen and obtained a precious tripod, the county was renamed Baoding.

sentences.zh: 漢皮氏縣，後魏改為龍門。

translations.literal: Han Pishi County; in Later Wei it was changed to Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: The Han county of Pishi; in Later Wei it was renamed Longmen.

sentences.zh: ，於縣置泰州，領龍門、萬泉、汾陰四縣。

translations.literal: , at the county Tai Prefecture was established, overseeing Longmen, Wanquan, and Fenyin—four counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Tai Prefecture was established at the county seat, governing Longmen, Wanquan, and Fenyin.

sentences.zh: ，廢泰州及芮縣，以龍門、萬泉屬絳州，汾陰屬蒲州

translations.literal: , Tai Prefecture and Rui County were abolished; Longmen and Wanquan were placed under Jiang Prefecture, and Fenyin under Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Tai Prefecture and Rui County were abolished; Longmen and Wanquan went to Jiang Prefecture and Fenyin to Pu.

translations.literal: A Han county.
translations.idiomatic: A Han county.

translations.literal: Under the Sui it was Tongxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui it was Tongxiang County.

translations.literal: , Wenxi County was established by detachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Wenxi County was established by division.

sentences.zh: ，分稷山界于薛通城置萬泉縣，屬泰州。

translations.literal: , Wanquan County was established on the border of Jishan at Xuetong Fortress and placed under Tai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Wanquan County was created on the Jishan border at Xuetong Fortress and assigned to Tai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州廢，入絳州，後又隸河中府。

translations.literal: When the prefecture was abolished, it entered Jiang Prefecture; later it was again subordinate to the Hedong Superior Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture was abolished it passed to Jiang Prefecture; later it came under Hedong Superior Prefecture.

translations.literal: Jiang Prefecture: Sui Jiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Prefecture: in Sui times the Jiang commandery.

sentences.zh: ，置絳州總管府，管絳、潞、蓋、建、澤、沁、韓、晉、呂、舉、泰、蒲、虞、芮、邵十五州。

translations.literal: , the Jiang Prefecture Superintendency was established, overseeing Jiang, Lu, Gai, Jian, Ze, Qin, Han, Jin, Lü, Ju, Tai, Pu, Yu, Rui, and Shao—fifteen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, a superintendency for Jiang Prefecture was set up over fifteen prefectures including Jiang, Lu, Gai, Jian, Ze, Qin, Han, Jin, Lü, Ju, Tai, Pu, Yu, Rui, and Shao.

sentences.zh: 絳州領正平、太平、曲沃、聞喜、稷山五縣。

translations.literal: Jiang Prefecture oversaw Zhengping, Taiping, Quwo, Wenxi, and Jishan—five counties.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Prefecture governed Zhengping, Taiping, Quwo, Wenxi, and Jishan.

translations.literal: In the third year, the superintendency was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wude the superintendency was abolished.

sentences.zh: 其年，以廢北澮州之翼城置翼城縣。

translations.literal: That same year, Yicheng County was established from Yicheng of the abolished Northern Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yicheng County was created from Yicheng of the abolished Northern Huan Prefecture.

translations.literal: It oversaw Yicheng, Jiang, and Xiaoxiang—three counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed Yicheng, Jiang, and Xiaoxiang.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude it was renamed Huan Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the second year, it was changed to Northern Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year it became Northern Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，州廢，三縣併入絳州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the prefecture was abolished and the three counties were merged into Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the prefecture was abolished and all three counties were merged into Jiang.

translations.literal: Southern Jiang Prefecture was established, and Jiang County was also established.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Jiang Prefecture was established, along with Jiang County.

sentences.zh: 漢絳縣地，後魏置曲沃縣

translations.literal: Territory of Han Jiang County; in Later Wei Quwo County was established.
translations.idiomatic: On the ground of Han Jiang County; in Later Wei, Quwo County was established.

sentences.zh: 漢聞喜縣，後魏置南絳州，又置絳縣

translations.literal: Han Wenxi County; in Later Wei Southern Jiang Prefecture was established, and Jiang County was also established.
translations.idiomatic: The Han county of Wenxi; in Later Wei Southern Jiang Prefecture was set up, and Jiang County was also established.

sentences.zh: 後魏高涼縣，隋改名稷山

translations.literal: Later Wei Gaoliang County; under the Sui it was renamed Jishan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Gaoliang County; under the Sui it was renamed Jishan.

translations.literal: A Sui county.
translations.idiomatic: A county of Sui times.

sentences.zh: ，置邵原，領垣、王屋，又置清廉、亳城四縣。

translations.literal: , Shaoyuan was established, overseeing Yuan and Wangwu, and Qinglian and Bocheng—four counties were also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yining, Shaoyuan was established over Yuan and Wangwu, with Qinglian and Bocheng also created.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude it was renamed Shao Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the second year, Changquan County was also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Changquan County was also established.

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Bocheng was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wude, Bocheng was abolished.

sentences.zh: 九年，省邵州，省清廉入垣縣，王屋屬懷州，垣屬絳州

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Shao Prefecture was abolished; Qinglian was abolished and merged into Yuan County; Wangwu belonged to Huai Prefecture and Yuan to Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Wude, Shao Prefecture was abolished; Qinglian was merged into Yuan, Wangwu went to Huai Prefecture, and Yuan to Jiang.

translations.literal: Later Wei Qinsheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Qinsheng County.

translations.literal: It was changed to Xiangling, taking the old Han name.
translations.idiomatic: It was renamed Xiangling, reviving the old Han name.

translations.literal: It belonged to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It belonged to Jin Prefecture.

translations.literal: , it belonged to Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe it was assigned to Jiang Prefecture.

translations.literal: Jin Prefecture: Sui Linfen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Prefecture: in Sui times the Linfen commandery.

sentences.zh: 義旗初，改為平陽郡，領臨汾、襄陵、岳陽、冀氏、楊五縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the righteous banner, it was changed to Pingyang Commandery, overseeing Linfen, Xiangling, Yueyang, Jishi, and Yang—five counties.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Tang cause it became the Pingyang commandery, governing Linfen, Xiangling, Yueyang, Jishi, and Yang.

translations.literal: That same year, Yang County was changed to Hongtong.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Yang County was renamed Hongtong.

sentences.zh: ，改為晉州，分襄陵置浮山縣，分洪洞置西河縣。

translations.literal: , it was changed to Jin Prefecture; Fushan County was established by detaching from Xiangling, and Xihe County by detaching from Hongtong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude it became Jin Prefecture; Fushan was split off from Xiangling and Xihe from Hongtong.

sentences.zh: 三年，置總管府，管晉、絳、沁、呂四州。

translations.literal: In the third year, a superintendency was established, overseeing Jin, Jiang, Qin, and Lü—four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year a superintendency was established over Jin, Jiang, Qin, and Lü.

translations.literal: The seat of administration was moved to Baima Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: The seat was moved to Baima Fortress.

translations.literal: Fushan was changed to Shenshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Fushan was renamed Shenshan County.

translations.literal: , the military commissioner was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Wude the regional commissioner was abolished.

sentences.zh: 十二年，移治所於平陽古城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the seat of administration was moved to the old city of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhenguan the seat was moved to the old city of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 十七年，省西河縣，以廢呂州之霍邑、趙城、汾西三縣來屬。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Xihe County was abolished; Huoyi, Zhaocheng, and Fenxi from the abolished Lü Prefecture were placed under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Xihe was abolished and Huoyi, Zhaocheng, and Fenxi from the abolished Lü Prefecture were added.

translations.literal: , the prefecture was changed to Pingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao the prefecture was renamed the Pingyang commandery.

translations.literal: , it was restored as Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan it again became Jin Prefecture.

translations.literal: , Xiangling was detached to belong to Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, Xiangling was transferred to Jiang Prefecture.

translations.literal: , it was changed to belong to the Hedong Superior Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangde it was placed under Hedong Superior Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣七，戶二萬一千六百一十七，口九萬七千五百五。

translations.literal: Formerly it oversaw seven counties, with 21,617 households and 97,505 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly it governed seven counties, with 21,617 households and 97,505 persons.

sentences.zh: 天寶領縣九，戶六萬四千八百三十六，口四十二萬九千二百二十一。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao it oversaw nine counties, with 64,836 households and 429,221 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao it governed nine counties, with 64,836 households and 429,221 persons.

translations.literal: Under Yuanhe it oversaw eight counties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanhe it governed eight counties.

sentences.zh: 在京師東北七百二十五里，至東都七百三十九里。

translations.literal: It lay 725 li northeast of the capital and 739 li to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It stood 725 li northeast of Chang'an and 739 li from Luoyang.

translations.literal: Han Pingyang County; under the Sui it was changed to Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: The Han county of Pingyang; under the Sui it was renamed Linfen.

translations.literal: , Xihe County was abolished and merged into Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Xihe County was abolished and merged into Linfen.

translations.literal: Han Yang County; under the Sui the name was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The Han county of Yang; the name remained unchanged through the Sui.

sentences.zh: 義甯元年，改為洪洞，取縣北嶺名

translations.literal: In the first year of Yining, it was changed to Hongtong, taking the name of the ridge north of the county.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yining it was renamed Hongtong, after the ridge north of the county seat.

translations.literal: , Fushan County was established by detaching from Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Fushan County was split off from Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 四年，改為神山，以縣東南羊角山神見為名

translations.literal: In the fourth year, it was changed to Shenshan, taking its name from the manifestation of a deity at Horn Mountain southeast of the county.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude it was renamed Shenshan, after a divine manifestation at Horn Mountain southeast of the county.

sentences.zh: 後魏安澤縣，隋改為岳陽

translations.literal: Later Wei Anze County; under the Sui it was changed to Yueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Anze County; under the Sui it was renamed Yueyang.

translations.literal: Han Zhi County; in Later Han it was changed to Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Han county of Zhi; in Later Han it was renamed Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 隋於此置汾州，尋改為呂州，領霍邑、趙城、汾西、靈石四縣。

translations.literal: Under the Sui Fen Prefecture was established here, soon changed to Lü Prefecture, overseeing Huoyi, Zhaocheng, Fenxi, and Lingshi—four counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui first placed Fen Prefecture here, then renamed it Lü Prefecture, governing Huoyi, Zhaocheng, Fenxi, and Lingshi.

sentences.zh: ，廢呂州，以霍邑等三縣來屬，以靈石屬汾州

translations.literal: , Lü Prefecture was abolished; Huoyi and the other three counties came under its jurisdiction, and Lingshi belonged to Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Lü Prefecture was abolished; Huoyi and two other counties were added here, while Lingshi went to Fen Prefecture.

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty, it was established by detaching from Huoyi County.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty, the county was split off from Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 後漢汾西郡，隋廢為縣，屬呂州。

translations.literal: Later Han Fenxi Commandery; under the Sui it was abolished to a county and belonged to Lü Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han Fenxi commandery; under the Sui it was reduced to a county under Lü Prefecture.

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui it fell to rebels.

translations.literal: From after the Zhide era, the Central Plains saw many troubles; common people of Xiang and Deng and the gentry of the two capitals all fled to the Jiang and Xiang regions. sentences.zh: 漢魚復縣，屬巴郡，今縣北三里赤甲城是也。

translations.literal: In Han times it was Yufu County, belonging to Ba Commandery; the present site is Chijia City, three li north of the county.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times it was Yufu County in Ba commandery; the present county seat is at Chijia City, three li to the north.

sentences.zh: 梁置信州，周為永安郡，隋為巴東郡，仍改為人復縣。

translations.literal: Liang established Xin Prefecture; under Zhou it was Yong'an Commandery; under the Sui it was Badong Commandery, and it was still changed to Renfu County.
translations.idiomatic: Liang established Xin Prefecture; under Zhou it was Yong'an commandery; under the Sui it was Badong commandery and was renamed Renfu County.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Fengjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Zhenguan it was renamed Fengjie.

translations.literal: In Han times it was Qu County, belonging to Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times it was Qu County in Ba commandery.

translations.literal: The old city was called Ten-Thousand-Household City.
translations.idiomatic: Its old city was called Ten-Thousand-Household City.

translations.literal: Thirty li west of the county there is a salt office.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li west of the county there is a salt office.

translations.literal: In Han times it was Wu County, belonging to Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times it was Wu County in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋加「山」字，以巫山硤為名。

translations.literal: Under the Sui the character "mountain" was added, named for Wushan Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui added the character for "mountain," naming it after Wushan Gorge.

translations.literal: Formerly administered at Wuzi City.
translations.idiomatic: Its former seat was at Wuzi City.

sentences.zh: 晉分巫、秭歸縣置建昌縣，又改為大昌。

translations.literal: Under Jin, Jianchang County was established by division from Wu and Zigui counties, and was again changed to Dachang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin split off Jianchang County from Wu and Zigui, later renaming it Dachang.

translations.literal: Under the Sui it was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui left the name unchanged.

sentences.zh: 萬州隋巴東郡之南浦縣。

translations.literal: Wan Prefecture: under the Sui it was Nanpu County of Badong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Prefecture: in Sui times it was Nanpu County in the Badong commandery.

sentences.zh: ，割信州之南浦置南浦州，領南浦、梁山、武寧三縣。

translations.literal: , Nanpu of Xin Prefecture was cut off and Nanpu Prefecture was established, overseeing Nanpu, Liangshan, and Wuning—three counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Nanpu was detached from Xin Prefecture to form Nanpu Prefecture, governing Nanpu, Liangshan, and Wuning.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢南浦州，以南浦、梁山屬夔州，武寧屬臨州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Nanpu Prefecture was abolished; Nanpu and Liangshan were placed under Kuizhou, and Wuning under Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Wude, Nanpu Prefecture was abolished; Nanpu and Liangshan went to Kuizhou and Wuning to Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其年，復立浦州，依舊領三縣。

translations.literal: That same year, Pu Prefecture was re-established, still overseeing the three counties as before.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Pu Prefecture was restored, again governing the three counties.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Wan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude it was renamed Wan Prefecture.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Nanpu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao it was renamed the Nanpu commandery.

sentences.zh: ，復為萬州，舊領縣三，戶五千三百九十六，口三萬八千八百六十七。

translations.literal: , it was restored as Wan Prefecture; formerly it oversaw three counties, with 5,396 households and a population of 38,867.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan it was restored as Wan Prefecture; formerly it governed three counties, with 5,396 households and 38,867 persons.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶五千一百七十九，口二萬五千七百四十六。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao: 5,179 households and 25,746 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao it had 5,179 households and 25,746 persons.

sentences.zh: 在京師西南二千六百二十四里，至東都二千四百六十五里。

translations.literal: It lay 2,624 li southwest of the capital and 2,465 li to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 2,624 li southwest of the capital and 2,465 li from the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 後魏分朐縣置魚泉縣，周改為萬川，隋改為南浦。

translations.literal: Later Wei established Yuquan County by division from Qu County; Zhou changed it to Wanchuan; under the Sui it was changed to Nanpu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei split Yuquan County off from Qu; Zhou renamed it Wanchuan, and the Sui renamed it Nanpu.

translations.literal: , Pu Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Pu Prefecture was established.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Wan Prefecture, with this county as the seat of administration.
translations.idiomatic: When it was renamed Wan Prefecture, this county became the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 漢臨江縣地，周分置源陽縣，隋改為武甯，治巴子故城

translations.literal: It was the territory of Han Linjiang County; Zhou established Yuanyang County by division; under the Sui it was changed to Wuning, administered at the old city of the Ba lord.
translations.idiomatic: It was the territory of Han Linjiang County; Zhou split off Yuanyang County; the Sui renamed it Wuning, with its seat at the old city of the Ba lord.

sentences.zh: 後周分朐縣置，治後魏萬川郡故城。

translations.literal: Later Zhou established it by division from Qu County, administered at the old city of Later Wei's Wanchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou split it off from Qu County, with its seat at the old city of Later Wei's Wanchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 忠州隋巴東郡之臨江縣。

translations.literal: Zhong Prefecture: under the Sui it was Linjiang County of Badong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Prefecture: in Sui times it was Linjiang County in the Badong commandery.

translations.literal: , Lin Prefecture was established, and Fengdu County was also established by division.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Lin Prefecture was established and Fengdu County was split off.

sentences.zh: ，分浦州之武甯置南賓縣，又分臨江置清水縣，並屬臨州。

translations.literal: , Nanbin County was established by division from Wuning of Pu Prefecture, and Qingshui County was established by division from Linjiang; both belonged to Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Nanbin County was split off from Wuning in Pu Prefecture, and Qingshui County from Linjiang; both were placed under Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八年，又以浦州之武寧來屬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Wuning of Pu Prefecture again came to belong to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Wude, Wuning from Pu Prefecture was again assigned to it.

translations.literal: That same year, it was again subordinate to Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That same year it was again placed under Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九年，以廢濆州之墊江來屬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Dianjiang of the abolished Fen Prefecture came to belong to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Wude, Dianjiang from the abolished Fen Prefecture was assigned to it.

translations.literal: , Lin Prefecture was changed to Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wude, Lin Prefecture was renamed Zhong Prefecture.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Nanbin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao it was renamed the Nanbin commandery.

translations.literal: , it was restored as Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan it was restored as Zhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊領縣五，戶八千三百一十九，口四萬九千四百七十八。

translations.literal: Formerly it oversaw five counties, with 8,319 households and a population of 49,478.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly it governed five counties, with 8,319 households and 49,478 persons.

sentences.zh: 天寶，戶六千七百二十二，口四萬三千二十六。

translations.literal: Under Tianbao: 6,722 households and 43,026 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao it had 6,722 households and 43,026 persons.

sentences.zh: 在京師南二千二百二十二里，至東都二千七百四十七里。

translations.literal: It lay 2,222 li south of the capital and 2,747 li to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 2,222 li south of the capital and 2,747 li from the Eastern Capital.

translations.literal: A Han county, belonging to Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A Han county under Ba commandery.

translations.literal: Later Wei established Wanchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei established Wanchuan commandery.

translations.literal: , Lin Prefecture was changed to Zhong Prefecture, and administration was at this county.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Prefecture was renamed Zhong Prefecture, this county became the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: It was the territory of Han Zhi County, belonging to Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: It was the territory of Han Zhi County in Ba commandery.

translations.literal: Later Han established Pingdu County.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han established Pingdu County.

translations.literal: , Fengdu County was established by division from Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Fengdu County was split off from Linjiang.

translations.literal: , it was established by division from Wuning County.
translations.idiomatic: It was established by division from Wuning County.

translations.literal: A Han county, belonging to Ba Commandery; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: A Han county in Ba commandery, later abolished.

translations.literal: Later Wei re-established it by division from Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei restored it by splitting it off from Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 周改為魏安，隋復為墊江。

translations.literal: Zhou changed it to Wei'an; under the Sui it was restored as Dianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou renamed it Wei'an; the Sui restored the name Dianjiang.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, it belonged to Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude it belonged to Fen Prefecture.

translations.literal: When the prefecture was abolished, it belonged to Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Fen Prefecture was abolished, it was placed under Lin Prefecture.

translations.literal: , Qingshui County was established by division from Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshui County was split off from Linjiang.

translations.literal: , it was changed to Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao it was renamed Guixi.
